passage: Monday: Tejas teased his sister Diya about her missing front tooth until she squealed. Wednesday: At the park, Hrithik from the next lane shoved Diya off the swing, and she landed on her hands. Tejas dropped his bat and ran. He stood in front of her and said, "Don't touch my sister." His voice shook, but his fists stayed open. He took Diya's hand, walked her home and told Papa what happened. Friday: Tejas was calling Diya "gap-tooth" again, but he gave her the bigger half of his biscuit while he did it.

qa.q: Who shoved Diya off the swing?
qa.a: Hrithik from the next lane shoved her off the swing.

qa.q: Why did Tejas stand in front of Diya even though he teases her himself?
qa.a: He may tease her, but she is his sister, and he felt protective when someone else hurt her.

qa.q: What did Tejas do after defending Diya that kept things from turning violent?
qa.a: He took her hand, walked her home and told Papa instead of hitting Hrithik.

qa.q: How might Diya see Tejas after the swing incident?
qa.a: Diya probably feels safe and cared for because her brother stood up for her, even though he still teases her a little.

grounding: A sibling who teases his sister still defends her from an outsider, then tells a parent without violence.

passage:
Note from the after-school club leader, Wednesday.
Disha usually teases her little sister Mehak: she mocks her lisp and calls her "tortoise" when she's slow. Today, though, a bigger boy pushed Mehak off the slide, and she scraped her knee.
Disha dropped her book and ran over. She stood in front of Mehak and said firmly, "Don't touch my sister." She didn't push or shout back.
Then she brought Mehak straight to me. We cleaned the scrape, and I spoke to the boy. At pick-up Disha told their mother what had happened, holding Mehak's hand the whole time.

qa.q: What did the bigger boy do to Mehak?
qa.a: He pushed her off the slide.

qa.q: How did Disha feel when she saw Mehak pushed?
qa.a: She felt protective and angry on Mehak's behalf, dropping her book and running over.

qa.q: What did Disha do that was wise?
qa.a: She stood in front of Mehak and spoke firmly without violence, then brought her to the club leader and told their mother.

qa.q: How might Mehak feel with Disha standing in front of her?
qa.a: Mehak likely felt protected and safe, knowing her sister was on her side even though she teases her.

grounding: A girl who teases her little sister stands up for her when another child pushes her, then tells an adult and her parent without using violence.

passage:
Tuesday
I tease Rubina all the time. I call her "chipmunk" because of her cheeks. But today at the park, Ishita from Block C shoved her off the swing and she fell in the mud.
Something went hot inside me. I ran over and stood between them. "Leave my sister alone!" I didn't hit Ishita, even though I wanted to.
Ishita walked off. Rubina was crying. I helped her up and wiped her face.
At home I told Ammi. She hugged us both and said she'd talk to Ishita's mother tomorrow.
I still think Rubina's cheeks are funny. But nobody else gets to hurt her.
Nazia

qa.q: What does Nazia call Rubina when teasing her?
What did Nazia feel when Ishita shoved Rubina?
qa.a: Nazia felt a hot rush of anger and protectiveness.

qa.q: What did Nazia do instead of hitting Ishita?
qa.a: Nazia stood between them, told Ishita to leave, helped Rubina up and told Ammi at home.

qa.q: How might Rubina feel knowing Nazia stood up for her?
qa.a: Rubina may feel comforted and safe, seeing that her sibling is on her side.

grounding: Nazia teases a younger sister but defends her when another child pushes her, then tells their mother without using violence.
